description: Quantizes to a chord rather than a scale, stepping through a sequence of up to sixteen chords written as Roman numerals

params.text: Moves to the next chord, wrapping to the first after the last step
Sets how many chords are played before the sequence wraps, 1 to 16
Chooses the key the Roman numerals are read in: the first setting shifts nothing and each step above it adds a semitone, up to eleven
Chooses which of the ten stored chord sequences is played, 1 to 10

inputs.text: The voltage to quantize, one note per polyphonic channel
Moves to the next chord on each rise past 2V
Returns to the first chord on each rise past 2V
Added to both outputs in volts before they are clamped to -10V and +10V, a volt an octave
Nothing in the module reads this jack; the sequence is chosen by the PTTERN knob alone

outputs.text: The root note of the current chord as a pitch, one channel
The quantized notes, with as many channels as the input

notes: each of the sixteen squares stands for one step of the sequence and shows its chord; the chords themselves are set from the panel menu, not by clicking a square
the quantizing is uniform rather than nearest-note: each octave of input is cut into equal bands, one per note of the chord, so a rising ramp gives an evenly timed arpeggio
a new module starts with I, IV, V and I in the first four steps of the first sequence; every other slot holds a major I
menu: Set Step 1 Chord — chooses the Roman numeral and then the quality of the chord in the first step, and there is one of these items for each of the sixteen steps
